data.narrative:
ADASI, a sovereign-funded defense and security platform acquired by EDGE Group, occupies a specialized segment within a sector comprising 26 identifiable peers. The comparable universe includes 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private entities, with notable private benchmarks including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable in this case. The Defense & Security sector, while containing 26 same-sector peers, yielded insufficient comparable datapoints meeting stage-specific and tier-specific filters. Zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-valuation-tier comparables met the minimum threshold of three observations required for robust median derivation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given ADASI's specialized positioning and sovereign funding structure, which typically operates under distinct valuation dynamics than commercial private markets.

The absence of a tight peer set reflects the fragmentation of frontier defense-tech—where funding source (sovereign vs. venture), regulatory environment, and customer concentration diverge sharply across the comp universe. Alternative methods (DCF, transaction multiples, or strategic premium analysis) would require proprietary cash flow, revenue, or acquisition-related data not present in the available dataset. Valuation synthesis is therefore constrained; quantitative triangulation cannot be completed with the current information, and any point estimate would lack analytical foundation.
